Mix some snap caps into your magazines for training. If you're not familiar, they're inert cartridges that you can load into your magazine. When they come up, it's an opportunity to practice the response to clear the problem and keep shooting.

Immediate action for a stoppage: Tap, Rack, Bang. You TAP on the magazine to ensure it's firmly seated, RACK the slide or bolt (depending on weapons system) to allow for ejection and chambering of the next round, squeeze the trigger and hope for a BANG.

Only takes a few seconds and, in many common failure-to-fire scenarios, will resolve the issue and get you back in the fight. If tap/rack/bang doesn't do it, find cover and troubleshoot as soon as is practical.
Snap caps are also good for detecting bad shootimg habits, like pushing or anticipating recoil.

Definitely a useful diagnostic/training tool. Sometimes if I'm out on the range with a friend, we'll load each other's magazines (not a homoerotic euphemism) and incorporate snap caps so it's a bit less predictable if/when the situation comes up.

I know it's not going to make me into John Wick but working on stuff like that just makes me more confident in my ability to defend myself (should the need arise). Also, while I don't anticipate ever getting bored with the simple pleasure of target shooting, this just keeps it from becoming routine. Predictability leads to complacency and complacency kills.
